rules: First spoken word is the hook keyword (date, name, or claim) — zero greetings or filler.
On-screen text ≤ 6 words, high-contrast, appears at frame 0 and mirrors the first spoken phrase.
Camera static or ultra-slow zoom only; first hard cut at ≥ 2.5 s.
Voice starts at frame 0 with background music bed already audible.
Visual is either: (a) cinematic establishing shot, (b) creator medium shot in warm studio, or (c) split-screen illustration + creator.
Hook type must be one of: myth-bust, shock-fact/urgency, interactive-challenge, mystery-tease.
First sentence ends on a cliffhanger (incomplete thought) to force retention past 3 s.
No logos, watermarks, channel names, or CTAs in first 2 s.
Aspect ratio 9:16; text placed in title-safe zone (center 80%).

patterns.example: main aapko aadhi aadhi line bol raha hu

avoid: Fast cuts, pans, or motion in the first 2 s.
Generic retention bait ("watch till end", "comment below").
On-screen text longer than 6 words or appearing after frame 0.
distil.summary: Top performers open with immediate voice delivering a specific, high-stakes hook word-for-word on screen, over a static cinematic or creator shot with zero cuts for 2.5+ seconds. The first sentence is deliberately incomplete to compel the viewer past the 3-second mark.

rules: First audio (voiceover, SFX, or music) starts at frame 0 — zero silence.
On-screen text appears at frame 0, ≤ 5 words, high-contrast, center or top-third.
First spoken word is a proper noun (name, place, date) or 'The victim's' — no greetings, no 'hello', no 'aaj'.
First visual is either a split-screen (3D animation top + presenter bottom) OR a single high-stakes image (hospital, street, presenter close-up) — no generic b-roll.
First cut ≤ 2.0 s for videos targeting > 8 M views; ≤ 4.0 s otherwise.
Hook promises a specific, verifiable claim (celebrity conflict, crime detail, conspiracy date) within the first spoken sentence.
Presenter (if visible) makes direct eye contact, neutral-to-serious expression, no smiling.
Background audio matches tone: news-style VO for celebrity/crime, ominous music for mystery, distress SFX for victim stories.
No lower-thirds, watermarks, or channel branding in frames 0–60.

patterns.example: Varanasi ki ek tang gali mein
Ayan Pathan naam ke is ladke ne

avoid: Generic greetings or channel intros ('namaste dosto', 'welcome back')
Silent or music-only starts without voice/SFX at frame 0
First cut after 4 s unless the single shot is a high-stakes visual with immediate distress audio
On-screen text longer than 5 words or appearing after frame 0
Smiling presenter, casual posture, or busy background in the cold open
distil.summary: Top performers (48M combined) use a split-screen 3D animation + presenter template with a ≤1 s cut, immediate news-tone VO, and a proper-noun-first hook. All six winners open with audio at frame 0, ≤5-word text on screen, and a specific, high-stakes claim — never a greeting.

rules: First spoken word is the Hindi hook keyword (subject noun or question starter), zero greetings or filler; voiceover begins at frame 0.
On-screen text ≤ 3 words, only if it is the exact hook phrase; appears at frame 0 and disappears by first cut.
First visual is a high-fidelity 3D asset of the core subject (weapon, vehicle, structure, mechanism) in motion or about to move; no 2D/cartoon for tech topics.
First cut ≤ 1.0 s for question/myth-bust hooks; ≤ 1.5 s for story/mystery hooks; camera or object motion triggers the cut.
Audio: signature sound effect (gunshot, whoosh, engine, explosion) at frame 0, instantly followed by voiceover; no music-only intro.
Zero branding, channel name, or title card in frames 0–2 s.
Hook sentence completes within first 2 s; grammar is colloquial Hindi (Hinglish allowed), present or past tense, no conditional politeness.
Visual demonstrates the central mechanism or conflict immediately (bullet firing, bridge panning, shell rotating, missile approaching).
avoid: Greeting or polite opener (namaste, hello, swagat hai, dosto).
Static title card, logo, or channel name before the hook visual.
Silence or music-only start; voiceover and SFX must hit at frame 0.
First cut later than 1.5 s on high-stakes visual hooks (weapons, vehicles, explosions).
distil.summary: Top Hindi tech Shorts open with a colloquial Hindi hook word at frame 0, paired with a moving 3D hero asset and a signature SFX, then cut within 1 second. They never waste frames on greetings, branding, 2D art, or silent buildup.
